disease_label_per_paper: Staphylococcus aureus prostatic abscess with acute urinary retention
presentation_summary: 53-year-old Indigenous Australian man presented to a remote hospital with acute urinary retention.
Past history included type 2 diabetes mellitus, chronic hepatitis B infection, recurrent skin and soft tissue infections, long-term kava use, crusted scabies, and a right great toe ulcer.
After initial self-discharge he was recalled when urine culture showed MRSA; urinary symptoms and suprapubic pain persisted, and he had left thigh pain with a large hypoechoic thigh collection.
Digital rectal examination showed a firm normal-sized prostate without tenderness, illustrating that DRE tenderness can be absent despite prostatic abscess.

Admission labs showed WBC 12.7 x 10^9/L, neutrophils 8.7 x 10^9/L, and CRP 65 mg/L; CT abdomen/pelvis showed multiple prostatic abscesses including a prominent left-base abscess and multiple apical loculations.

actual_treatment: oral clindamycin added for prostatic penetration

outcome.source_text_value: clinically improved; repeat imaging five months later showed complete resolution of prostatic abscess

quality_warnings: MRSA culture identity, susceptibility, prostate aspirate culture, and blood culture are confirmatory/non-ranking.
The non-tender normal-sized DRE is retained as rankable negative presentation evidence because acute prostatic abscess can have atypical DRE.
Concurrent thigh abscess and skin findings are preserved as non-ranking context to avoid forcing this acute prostatitis case into a staphylococcal bacteremia-only presentation.
